key_insight: A one-sided stability argument yields cut-position- and degree-independent constants with explicit p²/h scaling for normal-flux control and a sufficient Nitsche penalty.
engineering_relevance: The result supports stable high-order finite element analysis on unfitted meshes without requiring the mesh to conform to smooth exterior boundaries.
method: Use a patchwise H¹ projection to split the discrete solution into a polynomial and a stabilized residual.
Control the polynomial along inward segments in the physical domain and the residual on complete elements.
Avoid exponentially costly polynomial continuation and derive hp-error estimates.
evidence_signal: Translated-disk experiments show bounded normalized flux constants and penalty thresholds over tested degrees and cuts, with resolved convergence curves following predicted orders.
watch_item: The theory requires smooth exterior boundaries and a geometry-dependent mesh restriction, and loses half a degree power in energy error and a full power in L² error relative to best approximation.
paper_title: One-Sided $p$-Explicit Stability for High-Order Cut Finite Element Nitsche Methods
